observations:
Torah #238 does not contain any clusters of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text. The teaching is a single-paragraph aphorism consisting of one causal argument: when a third party encounters two disputants, he will instinctively agree with one of them because that person is closer to the third party's שָׁרֶשׁ (soul-root) — since no two people are alike, one disputant must inevitably stand in closer root-proximity to the observer, and from this proximity comes instinctive agreement.

The text uses no bechina formula at all ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', 'כנ"ל' equivalences are entirely absent). The concept of שָׁרֶשׁ is invoked as an established metaphysical postulate, not as the target of a bechina identification chain. All conceptual relationships in the text are causal (eitza type): closeness-to-shoresh PRODUCES agreement; the inequality of people CAUSES one to be closer than the other.

New package threshold requirement: 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent conceptual domain. Torah #238 has: zero explicit bechina statements, zero bechina edges in the dataset, and only one substantive concept (שרש) around which the teaching revolves. This falls far below the threshold for a new package.

Further note on good/evil mirror structure: Torah #238 presents no good/evil polarity structure at all. The teaching is phenomenological — it describes a neutral mechanism of human soul-alignment that operates regardless of whether the disputants or the third party are on the side of holiness or not. No evil mirror package is applicable.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. The bechina graph for Torah #238 is legitimately empty. The Torah's structure is causal/aphoristic rather than bechina-based, and no new package domain meets the required threshold of 3+ concepts with explicit bechina equivalences.
